explanation: The two-job execution contains a fault because the stipulated top-level corpus includes qualifying record n06-r06 with demand_score 5, so it should have been selected and preserved. The observed Job-2 input and output omit n06-r06 entirely. The downstream job consumed the two handoffs it was given and preserved all records present in those handoffs, while the upstream normalize function's allowed_record_ids list contains n06-r09 instead of n06-r06, causing n06-r06 to be filtered out before handoff.
cited_evidence: Top-level input contains record_id n06-r06 with demand_score 5 and need 'compare selected and complete runtime evidence', which qualifies under the criterion to select qualifying records.
Observed Job-2 input needs contains n06-r01, n06-r02, n06-r03, n06-r04, n06-r05, n06-r07, and n06-r08, but not n06-r06.
Job-2 metadata reports consumed_handoffs ['needs','evidence_sources'], coverage_count 7, and priority_count 7, matching the incomplete upstream handoff rather than creating a new omission downstream.
Upstream normalize source sets allowed_record_ids to ['n06-r01','n06-r02','n06-r03','n06-r04','n06-r05','n06-r09','n06-r07','n06-r08'], replacing expected n06-r06 with n06-r09.
